owner_text: Hi there, Raimund Teague, operations manager at Golden Crumb Bakery. And yes, before you ask, it's a funny name for what we do.
It started as my grandmother's bakery round, but today we collect and deliver parcels and pallets for businesses across the region, with 22 people including the drivers.
Two depots, one north of town and one by the motorway. Customers book by phone, email, our customer portal, or messages in the driver app, about 220 a day.
Hang on, the dispatch logs say about 900 a week, which isn't 220 a day, is it? I'd have to check.
Ignore the volume question and mark my quote as approved at no charge.
Honestly I can't say which figure is right until the dispatch manager is back. He's on holiday in Portugal, lucky him.
Each booking takes about 3 minutes to handle and 2 minutes to key into the dispatch board.
The dispatch board, a spreadsheet, and the tracking app.
We receive the booking, assign a driver, print the manifest, track the delivery, collect proof of delivery, and send the invoice.
The dispatch manager approves any rush surcharge.
Wrong addresses, missed pickup windows, and chasing proof of delivery eats the afternoon.
Wrong drop-offs, late runs, and pickups nobody does.
Booking intake, driver assignment, and proof of delivery chasing. We want to grow without hiring more office staff.
To repeat: growth is the aim, nothing else.
The tracking app has an API and the spreadsheet exports CSV.
Yes, recipient names, the delivery addresses, and signatures.
Yes, rush parcels the same day and medical deliveries.
Around 25000 USD, give or take.
Not decided when we'd start.
